* ci: stage npm releases instead of publishing from CI

The trusted publisher on each @standard-schema package is stage-only, so
publish.yml can put a version in npm's staged queue and nothing else. A
maintainer approves it with 2FA before it becomes installable, which is a
proof of presence no CI credential can supply.

Both npm jobs now run `npm stage publish` through OIDC on npm 11.15+, then
wait up to 350 minutes for the approval and print the approval commands to
the job summary. NODE_AUTH_TOKEN and continue-on-error are gone: the
NPM_TOKEN secret is deleted, and staging must fail loudly.

Each JSR job gates on its npm job so JSR never serves a version npm has not
approved, and skips a version JSR already carries so a re-run after a late
approval does not fail there.

npm does not understand the `workspace:` protocol that `pnpm publish`
resolved on its way out, so the stage script resolves it first. With that,
`npm pack` and `pnpm pack` produce identical tarballs for both packages.
